chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to give his wealth to his relatives?' He said, 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wills until death comes to him. Indeed, the owner of the wealth may do with his wealth whatever he wills as long as he is alive. If he wills, he may gift it; if he wills, he may give it in charity; and if he wills, he may keep it until death comes to him. If he bequeaths it, then he is not restricted to more than one-third, except that the excellence lies in not neglecting those he supports and not harming his heirs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the limit of bequest (wasiyyah) in Shia jurisprudence and can a man give all his wealth to relatives while alive?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the distinction between absolute ownership during one's lifetime and the restricted disposal rights upon death, emphasizing that the one-third limit for wills applies only to the bequest portion, not the entire estate. It highlights the Shia scholarly principle of balancing the owner's autonomy with the moral obligation to provide for dependents, ensuring that heirs are not left destitute. The narration underscores the flexibility in wealth management, allowing for gifts (hibah) or charity (sadaqah) without the one-third constraint, provided the owner is alive.
